# /etc/systemd/system/transparent-shard-server.service
[Unit]
Description=Transparent PIR shard retrieval worker
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
RuntimeDirectory=transparent-pir
RuntimeDirectory=transparent-pir
RuntimeDirectory=transparent-pir
Type=simple
# Bound to the VPC interface, not to loopback and not to the internet. The
# firewall opens 8093 to the coordinator tag alone, so the only thing that can
# reach this is the coordinator. It is deliberately not published: the
# wallet-facing API is not designed yet, and the upstream default is loopback
# for exactly that reason.
# /srv/transparent-pir/sets/transparent-shards-v7-full is substituted by deploy-transparent-shard.sh with
# the versioned directory the set was shipped to, the same way the Caddyfile's
# host is substituted. It is a path per published set rather than one directory
# rewritten in place, so a rollback that restores this unit also restores the
# set the restored binary was built to read. A set of another schema is refused
# at load, so pointing an old binary at a new set is an outage, and pointing it
# at the set it came with is not.
#
# One line on purpose. systemd honours backslash continuations, but nothing
# validates this file before `systemctl enable --now` runs it -- unlike the
# Caddyfile, which is validated while the old config is still serving -- so a
# mis-parse here is a failed start, and a failed start is a rollback onto a
# shard set the restored binary may not be able to read. The line is long; the
# alternative is a parsing surface with no check in front of it.
#
# 5368709120, 7G, 1 and
# --assignment /opt/transparent-pir/assignments/b188d7152b7a92906f60aa9276f1aa81928a2373f13f07fda8bae12bb247758b.json --worker-id transparent-pir-recent-01 --prune-excess --runtime-cache-dir /srv/transparent-pir/runtime-cache --runtime-cache-max-bytes 10737418240 are substituted the same way. A single-host pilot gets
# 8 GiB, 12G, one build slot and nothing extra; a fleet worker gets its
# roster's budgets and slots and
# `--assignment <file> --worker-id <id> --prune-excess`, under which it loads
# only its assigned tables, prewarms them, and reports ready only once warm.
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/transparent-shard-server --listen 0.0.0.0:8093 --shard-dir /srv/transparent-pir/sets/transparent-shards-v7-full --cache-bytes 5368709120 --build-slots 1 --query-slots 2 --assignment /opt/transparent-pir/assignments/b188d7152b7a92906f60aa9276f1aa81928a2373f13f07fda8bae12bb247758b.json --worker-id transparent-pir-recent-01 --prune-excess --runtime-cache-dir /srv/transparent-pir/runtime-cache --runtime-cache-max-bytes 10737418240 --control-socket /run/transparent-pir/control.sock --active-record /opt/transparent-publisher/active.json
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
User=root
LimitNOFILE=1048576
Environment=RUST_LOG=info

# Sized from measurement rather than copied from the Enhance worker's 2 GiB,
# which is a different table. A shard costs about 257 MiB resident (128.5 MiB
# per table segment: a 32 MiB u16 database plus three 32 MiB pack matrices).
#
# This is now a backstop rather than the only limit. The service holds a
# byte-bounded runtime cache -- 8 GiB above -- and refuses work it cannot make
# room for, so reaching this cap means the reservation is wrong rather than
# that the set grew. The 4 GiB between the two covers what the reservation
# deliberately does not count: allocator fragmentation, the transient plaintext
# each build reads, the shared parameters, and in-flight requests.
#
# Re-measure with `shard-residency` before raising --cache-bytes. Swap is off so
# a reservation that drifted low fails loudly here rather than degrading into
# thrash.
MemoryMax=7G
MemorySwapMax=0

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

transparent-pir-archive-01.unit:
# /etc/systemd/system/transparent-shard-server.service
[Unit]
Description=Transparent PIR shard retrieval worker
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
RuntimeDirectory=transparent-pir
RuntimeDirectory=transparent-pir
Type=simple
# Bound to the VPC interface, not to loopback and not to the internet. The
# firewall opens 8093 to the coordinator tag alone, so the only thing that can
# reach this is the coordinator. It is deliberately not published: the
# wallet-facing API is not designed yet, and the upstream default is loopback
# for exactly that reason.
# /srv/transparent-pir/sets/transparent-shards-v7-full is substituted by deploy-transparent-shard.sh with
# the versioned directory the set was shipped to, the same way the Caddyfile's
# host is substituted. It is a path per published set rather than one directory
# rewritten in place, so a rollback that restores this unit also restores the
# set the restored binary was built to read. A set of another schema is refused
# at load, so pointing an old binary at a new set is an outage, and pointing it
# at the set it came with is not.
#
# One line on purpose. systemd honours backslash continuations, but nothing
# validates this file before `systemctl enable --now` runs it -- unlike the
# Caddyfile, which is validated while the old config is still serving -- so a
# mis-parse here is a failed start, and a failed start is a rollback onto a
# shard set the restored binary may not be able to read. The line is long; the
# alternative is a parsing surface with no check in front of it.
#
# 51539607552, 56G, 1 and
# --assignment /opt/transparent-pir/assignments/143054ae445d09bc2502bc66af80ccf939b38fe8f6486a9ba29b3a38b07ecdf0.json --worker-id transparent-pir-archive-01 --prune-excess --runtime-cache-dir /srv/transparent-pir/runtime-cache --runtime-cache-max-bytes 103079215104 are substituted the same way. A single-host pilot gets
# 8 GiB, 12G, one build slot and nothing extra; a fleet worker gets its
# roster's budgets and slots and
# `--assignment <file> --worker-id <id> --prune-excess`, under which it loads
# only its assigned tables, prewarms them, and reports ready only once warm.
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/transparent-shard-server --listen 0.0.0.0:8093 --shard-dir /srv/transparent-pir/sets/transparent-shards-v7-full --cache-bytes 51539607552 --build-slots 1 --query-slots 2 --assignment /opt/transparent-pir/assignments/143054ae445d09bc2502bc66af80ccf939b38fe8f6486a9ba29b3a38b07ecdf0.json --worker-id transparent-pir-archive-01 --prune-excess --runtime-cache-dir /srv/transparent-pir/runtime-cache --runtime-cache-max-bytes 103079215104 --control-socket /run/transparent-pir/control.sock --active-record /opt/transparent-publisher/active.json
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10
User=root
LimitNOFILE=1048576
Environment=RUST_LOG=info

# Sized from measurement rather than copied from the Enhance worker's 2 GiB,
# which is a different table. A shard costs about 257 MiB resident (128.5 MiB
# per table segment: a 32 MiB u16 database plus three 32 MiB pack matrices).
#
# This is now a backstop rather than the only limit. The service holds a
# byte-bounded runtime cache -- 8 GiB above -- and refuses work it cannot make
# room for, so reaching this cap means the reservation is wrong rather than
# that the set grew. The 4 GiB between the two covers what the reservation
# deliberately does not count: allocator fragmentation, the transient plaintext
# each build reads, the shared parameters, and in-flight requests.
#
# Re-measure with `shard-residency` before raising --cache-bytes. Swap is off so
# a reservation that drifted low fails loudly here rather than degrading into
# thrash.
MemoryMax=56G
MemorySwapMax=0

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
